desc.gemma-4-e2b-it-qat-ud-q4-k-xl: Default. The lightest non-MTP Gemma 4 QAT preset, intended for the standard flow that summarizes before chat. Maximum context is 131k.
desc.gemma-4-e2b-it-qat-mtp-ud-q4-k-xl: The lightest Gemma 4 QAT MTP preset. It uses the same target GGUF plus a draft GGUF for speculative decoding. MTP often speeds up chat, but summary workloads are usually slower.
desc.gemma-4-e4b-it-qat-ud-q4-k-xl: Lightweight non-MTP Gemma 4 QAT preset for summary and chat workloads larger than E2B.
desc.gemma-4-e4b-it-qat-mtp-ud-q4-k-xl: Lightweight Gemma 4 QAT MTP preset. It uses the same target GGUF plus a draft GGUF for speculative decoding. MTP often speeds up chat, but summary workloads are usually slower.
desc.gemma-4-12b-it-qat-ud-q4-k-xl: Mid-size non-MTP Gemma 4 QAT preset for larger RAM environments with 256k context.
desc.gemma-4-12b-it-qat-mtp-ud-q4-k-xl: Mid-size Gemma 4 QAT MTP preset. The target is gemma-4-12B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf, and mtp-gemma-4-12b-it.gguf is only the draft model. Summary workloads are usually slower with MTP.
desc.qwen3-6-35b-a3b-mtp-ud-q4-k-m: MTP-capable Qwen3.6 MoE (active 3B). Same-file MTP needs no separate draft GGUF. MTP often speeds up chat, but summary workloads are usually slower.
desc.qwen3-6-27b-mtp-ud-q4-k-xl: MTP-capable Qwen3.6 27B for chat quality and long-context operation. Summary workloads are usually slower with MTP.
desc.qwen3-5-9b-mtp-ud-q4-k-xl: MTP-capable lightweight Qwen3.5 for everyday chat and short interactions. Summary workloads are usually slower with MTP.
desc.qwen3-5-122b-a10b-mtp-ud-q4-k-s: MTP-capable largest-scale Qwen3.5 MoE 122B (active 10B). A multi-shard, high-memory preset. Summary workloads are usually slower with MTP.
desc.qwen3-6-27b-ud-q4-k-xl: The most stable for Japanese summary / reflection / chat quality. Supports long context (262k). The actual RAM estimate changes with ctx_size and KV cache type.
desc.qwen3-6-35b-a3b-ud-iq4-nl: MoE (active 3B). A memory-efficient variant that delivers near-27B-dense quality from a comparatively small gguf. The actual RAM estimate changes with ctx_size and KV cache type.
desc.qwen3-5-9b-ud-q4-k-xl: Lightweight and fast Qwen3.5. Japanese quality sufficient for everyday chat and daily summaries. Lower ctx_size makes it easier to run on 16GB-class machines.
desc.gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-ud-iq4-nl: MoE (active 4B). A mid-size Gemma 4 with good Japanese responses. The actual RAM estimate changes with ctx_size and KV cache type.
desc.qwen3-5-122b-a10b-ud-iq4-xs: Largest scale. MoE 122B (active 10B). A flagship aiming for top quality. The gguf itself is large, so this targets high-memory machines.

desc.qwen3-vl-embedding-2b: A multimodal variant that embeds text and images into the same vector space. Use this if you want image search.
desc.qwen3-embedding-0-6b: Default. Lightweight and fast. Quality sufficient for everyday use with a small memory footprint.
desc.qwen3-embedding-4b: Mid-size, high quality. Supports long context (40k); summary and Japanese search accuracy stay stable. Image search is disabled.
desc.ruri-v3-310m-onnx-int8: Lightweight Ruri v3 for Japanese retrieval. Uses an INT8 ONNX model and retrieval-specific prefixes. Image search is disabled.

migrationBackup.title: Backup before database migration
migrationBackup.desc: When the memories database needs a migration at startup, the migration tool backs it up first. Startups that change nothing take no backup.
migrationBackup.enabledDescription: Turning this off lets the migration run on low-disk machines, but a failed migration can then not be undone.
migrationBackup.disabledWarning: If a migration fails without a backup, the database cannot be restored and you will have to start with a new empty data location.
migrationBackup.keepDescription: After a successful migration the tool deletes older backups beyond this count. With 0, the backup is kept only during the migration and deleted after it succeeds.
migrationBackup.keepInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {{max}} for the backups to keep.

code.unsupported_resource: The vector DB is not a local directory and cannot be backed up, so the migration was stopped. Check your settings.
code.insufficient_space: There is not enough free space to migrate. Free up disk space, then retry.

code.migration_failed: An error occurred during the migration. Retry the migration.
code.verify_failed: Verification after the migration failed. Lookback needs an update; check the logs.
code.bundle_invalid: The bundled migration tool is damaged or mismatched. Reinstall Lookback.
code.backup_incomplete: The backup to restore is incomplete. Check the logs.
code.backup_newer_than_tool: This backup was made by a newer version of Lookback and cannot be restored.
code.restore_failed: An error occurred during the restore, and the previous state was put back. Retry.
code.tool_unavailable: The migration tool could not be started. Reinstall Lookback.
code.tool_output_unrecognized: The migration tool ended without reporting a result. Retry the migration.

settings.title: Coding agent settings
settings.description: Edit execution profiles, mounts, and repository hosts. Execution readiness is independent of whether settings can be repaired.
settings.backendDisabled: The execution environment is not ready. Open How these settings are used to review the details.
settings.backendStatusNeutral: Execution backend status is not confirmed. Settings editing and connection diagnostics remain available.
settings.backendStatusHelp: This item is not confirmed by the legacy diagnostic. Execution availability is decided by the preflight check before a run.
settings.backendDiagnosticDescription: These codes are retained as information from the legacy diagnostic. Execution availability is decided by the preflight check before a run.
settings.backendStatusUnavailable: The execution backend status is unavailable.
settings.profileListDescription: Manage the image, CLI, and allowed repositories for each execution profile.
settings.profileListHelp: A profile groups the image, CLI, network, mounts, and allowed repositories used by a run. Open a row to review its details.
settings.profileListEmpty: No profiles are configured. Add one from a preset or manual settings.
settings.settingsHelpDescription: 1. Add a profile and configure the agent and execution image. 2. Register the Git connection; it is the source and publication target for repositories. 3. In the profile, choose the repositories it may use. 4. Confirm the dialog changes, then use Save and apply in the footer. 5. After saving, open Authentication and settings from the profile row to sign in to the CLI in the same environment. Mount roots are host folders allowed for sharing.
settings.repositoryHostCredentialsHelp: Enter only the opaque setting ID registered in credential_sources[].id in trusted-host.json. When left blank (unspecified), an existing reference for the same repository in the legacy trusted policy is inherited; if none exists, reads are anonymous and publication is unconfigured. Clearing the input does not guarantee removal of an inherited credential. Never enter the secret itself.
settings.sshCredentialsShort: Use selected SSH settings for host Git operations
settings.sshCredentialsHelp: SSH uses config, known_hosts, and identity files from the selected SSH directory (or an existing path for the same repository in the legacy trusted policy when unspecified) for host Git operations; they are not automatically shared into the guest. This settings screen does not register or select SSH keys and does not support SSH agents or interactive passphrases. Clearing the path only clears the input and does not guarantee removal of inherited authentication settings.
settings.nativeRepositoryApprovalsDescription: Choose the repositories and base branches that native execution may use. An empty list denies every repository.
settings.nativeRepositoryApprovalsHelp: This is separate from profile.allowedRepositories: it approves the repositories and base branches the native backend may actually check out. Enter one branch per line.
settings.nativeRepositoryApprovalsUnavailable: Editing is disabled because the existing native approvals could not be retrieved. Other host fields, such as SSH settings and credential IDs, remain editable.
settings.invalidNativeRepositoryApproval: Enter a valid repository and at least one base branch.
settings.nativeSetupHelp: This shows the execution backend registration as a diagnostic. Unregistered, package-mismatched, or unavailable states are never presented as usable. Approval is a CAS operation for the current revision and package fingerprint.
settings.nativeSetupPackageReady: The bundled execution package was verified.
settings.nativeSetupPackageDevelopment: Development package (staged from sources with uncommitted changes or a branch head). Release builds do not accept it.

nativeSetupUnavailableReason.package_missing: The execution package is not bundled. In development it is staged automatically when pnpm tauri dev starts; check the staging output in the launch log. For an installed app, reinstall it.
nativeSetupUnavailableReason.unsupported_platform: The execution environment is available only in the Linux (KVM) build of this app.
nativeSetupUnavailableReason.trusted_policy_unsafe: The native host policy in application data has an unsafe owner or permissions. Check the application data directory permissions.
nativeSetupUnavailableReason.trusted_policy_invalid: The native host policy or repository host settings cannot be read. Review the repository hosts and the approval list, then save.
nativeSetupUnavailableReason.storage_unavailable: Private storage for the execution environment could not be initialized. Check application data permissions and free space.
nativeSetupUnavailableReason.executor_unavailable: The bundled execution component could not verify its capabilities. Reinstall the app.
nativeSetupUnavailableReason.settings_unavailable: Coding agent settings cannot be loaded. Save the settings again.

settings.nativeSetupApprovalListUnset: Not configured — no per-host approval list has been saved yet. Separately from each profile's allowed repositories, the repositories the execution environment may check out must be approved per host.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalListEmpty: The approval list is empty, so the execution environment rejects every repository.
settings.nativeSetupPendingRepositories: Allowed by a profile but missing from the approval list
settings.nativeSetupAddedPending: Added to the approval list. Confirm with “Save and apply” at the bottom of the page. Base branches can be changed in the repository host editor.
settings.nativeSetupHostMissing: Host {{host}} is not registered. Add the repository host first.
settings.nativeSetupUnavailable: The native backend status is unavailable.
settings.nativeSetupInvalidated: The settings revision changed, so this native diagnostic is invalidated. Fetch the current state again.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalMeaning: Approving records the fingerprint of the bundled execution package (coding-agent-executor and runtime) in this app's settings. Afterwards, when an Issue is run, that package may check approved repositories out into a private workspace on this host and run the agent CLI inside the sandbox VM. Approval alone runs nothing.
settings.nativeSetupApprovedDetail: Approved: coding-agent-executor {{version}} (fingerprint {{fingerprint}}). Issue runs use this package.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmRecordsBody: Only this package's fingerprint is saved in the Coding agent settings. Nothing is executed, no network connection is made, no repository is fetched, and no credential is read.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmEnablesTitle: What the app may do after approval
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmEnablesWorkspa: When an Issue is run, this package's executor checks the repositories of the approval list (step 3) out into a private workspace on this host and starts the profile's agent CLI inside the bundled runtime's sandbox VM.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmEnablesPublish: Push a result branch or create a pull request when that is selected for an Issue.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmEnablesCheck: Run the policy and Git read stages of the repository host “Check settings and connection” action.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmLimitsNoAutost: Nothing starts automatically; each Issue run is started separately.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmLimitsApproval: Repositories missing from the approval list stay rejected.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmLimitsShell: The authentication and settings shell works independently of this approval.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalConfirmRevoke: A package update invalidates the approval and asks for re-approval. There is currently no Settings action to revoke an approval.
settings.nativeSetupError: Native backend approval failed. Check the settings revision and execution backend.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalInvalidatedReason: The settings revision changed. Refresh the diagnostic before approving.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalDirtyReason: Save or discard the current settings draft before approving the native backend.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalSavingReason: Wait for the current settings save to finish before approving the native backend.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalInProgressReason: A native backend approval request is already in progress.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalPackageMismatchReason: The protected host policy in application data pins a different package, so approval is not possible from Settings.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalUnavailableReason: Execution environment information is unavailable. Check that the execution component is installed.
settings.nativeSetupApprovalAlreadyApprovedReason: The native backend is already approved.

nativeSetupState.not_approved: Not approved — this package has not been approved yet. Choose “Approve native backend”.
nativeSetupState.reapproval_required: Re-approval required — the package changed since it was approved. Choose “Approve native backend” to approve the new package.
nativeSetupState.package_mismatch: Approval unavailable — the protected host policy in application data pins a different package. This cannot be repaired from Settings; reinstall the app or ask whoever installed the policy.
nativeSetupState.unavailable: Unavailable — the execution package cannot be verified, so approval is not possible.

settings.hostConfigurationRisk: “Share host settings” mounts the selected Codex/Claude settings directories writable into the sandbox VM. If an agent in the VM is hijacked (for example by prompt injection), binaries or settings it writes there (MCP server commands, hooks, notify commands, and so on) may run automatically on the host the next time you use Codex/Claude on the host, defeating the sandbox isolation. Use it only if you accept this risk; otherwise choose “App-private settings”.
settings.hostConfigurationDescription: Explicitly selected Codex/Claude directories are shared read/write; the Claude common settings file is an import source for the shared app-owned HOME. Tilde is not expanded; the absolute path from the input or picker is used as-is.
settings.hostConfigurationHelp: Selected directories are shared read/write; the Claude common settings file is privately copied into the shared app-owned HOME only on first use or when its source path changes. Later updates are never written back to the source. OS credential stores such as the Codex keyring or macOS Keychain and SSH agents are not shared automatically; sign in from the authentication and settings shell when needed. Sharing a directory alone does not guarantee authentication for every CLI.
settings.claudeSettingsFileHelp: Select a file such as ~/.claude.json as an optional import source for Claude common settings. On first use or when the source path changes, the backend copies it privately into the shared app-owned HOME; later CLI updates stay in that HOME and are never written back. This is separate from the ~/.claude/ directory, which remains a read/write shared directory. Clearing the field stops future imports but does not delete data already imported.
settings.hostConfigurationPrepareHomeHelp: A profile sharing host settings cannot use the dedicated-home button. The backend prepares the shared app-owned HOME automatically and uses the selected directories plus imported Claude settings for normal runs and the settings shell.
settings.hostConfigurationInvalid: Choose at least one absolute Codex or Claude directory. Tilde paths are not supported.
settings.hostConfigurationOpenCodeHelp: Host settings sharing is not supported for OpenCode profiles. Use app-private settings or select a supported Codex or Claude command.
settings.unregisteredRepositoryHost: This profile references an unregistered repository host. Review the profile
settings.unregisteredRepositoryHostHelp: Register the repository host or update the profile's allowed repositories. Activate this warning to open the editor.
settings.authenticationDialogDescription: Prepare the saved profile home, then sign in through a shell that uses the same environment. Credentials are reused by ordinary runs.
settings.profileIdentityHelp: The profile ID and version identify the saved contract and cannot be edited as ordinary fields.
settings.profileMountAvailabilityHelp: Review the allowed mount roots. This is information about preflight availability; settings editing can continue.
settings.confirmDiscardDialog: What should happen to these edits? Apply and close keeps this dialog draft in the list; discard and close loses the edits.
settings.setupDescription: Proceed in this order: save settings, prepare the dedicated home, then open the authentication and settings shell. This is separate from the execution backend probe.
settings.setupStepTerminal: Open the authentication and settings shell
settings.setupSaveDescription: This saves all settings, not only the profile. Prepare the home and use the shell after saving.
settings.setupHomeDescription: For first use, create a dedicated home for saved authentication and settings with the button. An existing writable home mount can also be shared with ordinary runs.
settings.setupTerminalDescription: Open the saved profile's authentication and settings shell. Shell operations remain manual.
settings.setupNoProfile: Choose a preset or add a profile above, then save the settings. The dedicated home and authentication and settings shell become available after saving.
settings.mountsUnavailable: Profile mounts are unavailable. Repair the profile and check again.
settings.imageRefHelp: Enter the pinned image reference used for execution. Use a reviewed reference instead of relying on a mutable tag.
settings.commandArgsHelp: Enter the CLI and its arguments, one item per line, for the image entrypoint. A blank command cannot be saved.
settings.containerHomeHelp: The guest-side home path used by the CLI during execution. It is also the location for saved authentication and settings.
settings.runtimeEnvironmentDescription: Set guest paths that keep CLI and Rust state separate from the image home. HOME and PATH cannot be changed. Empty values are removed when saved.
settings.runtimeEnvironmentHelp: Enter guest paths for CLI and Rust state. HOME and PATH cannot be changed.
settings.mountRootsHelp: Enter absolute host paths that may be shared with the execution environment, one per line. These are not guest paths.
settings.prepareHomeDescription: Create a persistent home for the saved profile's credentials and agent settings. An existing home mount can be used instead; remove conflicting shared mounts before preparing a dedicated home. Save your settings before proceeding.
settings.prepareHomeDirty: There are unsaved changes. Save the settings before preparing the dedicated home.
settings.prepareHomeSaving: Settings are being saved or the dedicated home is being prepared. Wait before trying again.
settings.prepareHomeError: Could not prepare the home. Check for conflicting mounts or a profile currently in use.
settings.setupHomeReady: Dedicated home: ready (a writable home mount exists)
settings.terminalDescription: Open a shell with the saved profile's image and home. Configure CLI login or settings in the terminal. This does not probe the execution backend or infer that authentication is complete.
settings.terminalReuseDescription: The shell uses the same image and shared home, so saved authentication and settings are reused by ordinary runs. Authentication success is not inferred automatically.
settings.terminalDirty: Save the profile settings first. The authentication and settings shell cannot open while changes are unsaved.
settings.terminalGuideCodex: For Codex, enter codex login in the terminal. CODEX_HOME inside the dedicated home is created automatically when the shell starts. Nothing is run automatically.
settings.terminalGuideClaude: For Claude, enter claude auth --help in the terminal to confirm the available authentication operation. No authentication command is run automatically.
settings.terminalGuideOpenCode: For OpenCode, enter opencode providers --help in the terminal to confirm provider and authentication operations. No authentication command is run automatically.
settings.terminalGuideGeneric: Use the selected command's help in the terminal, then enter CLI settings or authentication operations manually. Nothing is run automatically.
settings.terminalSaving: Profile settings are being saved. The authentication and settings shell is unavailable until saving finishes.
settings.terminalStarting: The authentication and settings shell is starting. A new session cannot open until it finishes.
settings.terminalListPending: Existing authentication and settings shells are being checked. Wait for the session list before starting one.
settings.terminalListError: Existing authentication and settings shells could not be checked. Retry to load the session list before starting one.
settings.terminalActiveSession: An existing authentication and settings shell is active. Confirm it has finished or been cancelled before starting another.
settings.terminalUnknownSession: An existing authentication and settings shell has an unknown state. Cancel the unresolved session before starting another.
settings.terminalCredentialReference: Profiles with a credential reference cannot open an authentication and settings shell because of a backend restriction. Remove the credential reference and save first.
settings.terminalHomeMissing: Prepare a writable home with “Prepare dedicated home” first. The authentication and settings shell cannot open without a home.
settings.terminalStartError: Could not start the terminal. Check the settings, mounts, runtime, and session list.
settings.terminalOperationError: Could not operate the terminal. Wait for confirmed completion before starting another session.
settings.allowedRepositoriesHelp: These are the repositories this profile may work on. Register the connection first, then enter one host/org/repository per line.
settings.invalidRepositories: Repositories must contain exactly host/org/repository. Extra path segments or empty parts cannot be saved or checked.
settings.invalidRepositoryHost: Enter the host name, API URL, and clone connection target.
settings.hostCheckDescription: Check saved host settings against the effective repository approvals and existing read-only authentication path. Save changes with the shared footer before checking. This never writes, creates PRs or Issues, or runs an agent.
settings.hostCheckStructuralOnly: Without a repository, only structural checks run.
settings.hostCheckReadOnlyScope: Results cover read-only checks for the selected settings and repository. Git success does not imply API authentication or write permission.
settings.hostCheckError: The repository host check failed. Detailed external errors are not displayed.
settings.hostCheckUnknownCode: Details for this check stage are unavailable.

hostCheckCodes.policy_matched: The effective repository approval policy matched.
hostCheckCodes.policy_missing: The effective repository approval policy is unavailable.
hostCheckCodes.policy_invalid: The effective repository approval policy is invalid.
hostCheckCodes.repository_not_approved: The repository is not an approved identity.
hostCheckCodes.native_backend_not_approved: Register the execution environment in Settings, then check the connection again.
hostCheckCodes.policy_mismatch: The repository or host settings do not match the effective approval policy.
hostCheckCodes.git_failed: The Git repository could not be read.
hostCheckCodes.forge_readable: Forge API authentication and repository read succeeded.
hostCheckCodes.forge_not_configured: The Forge API is not configured.
hostCheckCodes.credential_not_configured: An API credential is not configured.
hostCheckCodes.authentication_failed: Forge API authentication could not be confirmed.
hostCheckCodes.access_denied: The Forge API returned a permission or usage restriction.
hostCheckCodes.repository_not_found: The repository was not found or cannot be referenced.
hostCheckCodes.redirect_rejected: The connection rejected a redirect instead of following it.
hostCheckCodes.invalid_response: The Forge API response shape could not be confirmed.
hostCheckCodes.response_too_large: The response was too large, so the check stopped.
hostCheckCodes.unsupported_capability: The executor package does not support repository checks.
hostCheckCodes.prerequisite_failed: This stage was not checked because a prerequisite failed.

settings.credentialReferenceHelp: Enter only the opaque reference resolved by the backend, never the secret itself. The reference is shown and saved as configuration.
settings.profileRuntimeGroupHelp: Configure the home, environment variables, and network access used before an execution starts.
settings.profileFileSharingGroupHelp: Configure host roots and persistent mounts shared with the guest. Allow only the paths required by the run.
settings.profileAuthGroupHelp: Configure allowed images and the credential reference. Do not enter a secret value.
settings.profileResourcesGroupHelp: Configure CPU, memory, disk, and parallel-run limits. Values are validated as positive integers before saving.
settings.resources: CPU {{cpu}} millicores · Memory {{memory}} MiB · root disk {{disk}} MiB
settings.repositoryHostsDescription: Manage code sources and publication targets with transport and credential references.
settings.repositoryHostDraftHint: Unsaved changes prevent the connection check. The check runs against the saved settings, so save with “Save and apply” at the bottom of the page (or discard the changes) first.
settings.repositoryHostSavingHint: Saving settings. The connection check becomes available when the save finishes.
settings.repositoryHostsHelp: Connections to Git services used to fetch code and publish changes. Set the host, service, API URL, and transport, then run the connection check. Changes use the shared save and connection checks are read-only.
settings.hostInUse: This host is referenced by a profile and cannot be removed.

run.title: Coding agent
run.description: Review the backend's canonical plan and explicitly approve its digest. Backend responses are authoritative for execution state and blockers.

run.backendUnavailable: The execution environment is unavailable. Backend status could not be read.
run.settingsUnavailable: Coding agent settings could not be read.
run.noProfile: No execution profile is configured. Repair or add one in Settings.
run.profileMountUnavailable: Mounts for the selected profile are unavailable.
run.autoDoneNote: Defaults to OFF. Available when semantic judging and automatic completion are enabled. The same settings apply to investigation Issues.
run.noPromptReceipt: The API for automatic prompt delivery and CLI receipt confirmation is not connected. No automatic input or receipt claim is made.
run.validationCommands: Validation commands (one JSON argv array per line)
run.validationRequired: Require successful validation for automatic completion
run.validationMismatch: The returned plan does not match the requested validation commands. Refresh the plan.
run.validationInvalid: Enter JSON argv arrays, a directory inside /workspace, and a timeout from 1 to 10800 seconds.
run.planDetailsUnavailable: The native preview does not include the approved base commit or verification plan. Start remains blocked until those facts are bound to the approval digest.
run.finishUnavailable: Normal CLI exit and a verified graceful-finish capability are not available in the current run contract. Finish stays disabled.
run.repositoryCandidates: Repository candidates returned by the backend
run.notApprovable: The backend did not mark this plan approvable. It cannot be started.
run.planNeedsRefresh: Inputs changed. Fetch a new canonical plan before approval.
run.confirmDigest: Review the backend digest and Issue revision below.
run.manualRepositoryConfirm: I confirm this manual repository selection

run.heartbeatUnavailable: The execution heartbeat could not be confirmed.
run.ownerUnavailable: This run is owned by another application window. It was not cancelled.
run.runActionUnavailable: The run action could not be confirmed.
